stages.title: Evaluate ingestion, marking and Cloudflare backend architecture
stages.outcome: Select an architecture from representative ST2132 and CS2100 evidence, with measured marking limits and personal/pilot operating costs.
exit: Review a small representative pack covering multipart maths, proofs, MIPS, circuits, keyed choices and supporting source excerpts; use safe synthetic fixtures until private inputs are available.
Compare parsing/repair fidelity, source anchors, retrieval support and rubric/key handling; evaluate correct alternatives, partial work and justified abstention separately by format.
Decide service boundaries for identity, storage, durable imports/marking, retrieval and exam deadlines alongside the static Pages frontend; record tradeoffs in ADRs.
Define portable data/API contracts, quality gates, finite retries/model escalation, monthly cost assumptions and a path from personal to invited use.
questions: Which semester-specific instructions and trusted solutions are available?
Which typed/handwritten answer workflows and provisional marks are acceptable?
What is the owner's monthly budget and likely library/answer volume?
stages.nonGoals: Do not import an entire textbook, deploy infrastructure or choose providers without evidence. This stage is research/refinement, not permission to implement the whole backend.

stages.title: Design the quiet revision workspace and answer interactions
stages.outcome: Establish a beautiful, minimal study UI with brief copy and usable maths, code and diagram workflows.
exit: Refine navigation and module context, daily plan, question/working/feedback hierarchy and source evidence using synthetic scenarios.
Cover keyboard and narrow layouts, 200% zoom, long equations/code, circuit images and loading/empty/error/pending states.
Define semantic tokens, typography, spacing and a small set of reusable interaction patterns without an oversized component framework.
Obtain human visual feedback on the affected desktop/mobile scenarios; record accepted decisions and performance goals.
questions: What is the most comfortable proof-working and circuit-input workflow?
Which study interactions need side-by-side evidence versus progressive disclosure?
stages.nonGoals: No marketing site, decorative metrics, exhaustive design system or production data integration. The current starter is a direction, not final UI acceptance.

stages.title: Create private module offerings and versioned exam profiles
stages.outcome: The owner can securely create ST2132/CS2100 offerings, define examinable skills and configure each assessment's rules.
exit: Implement the chosen identity/session and ownership model end to end, with two isolated module offerings and no public-source defaults.
Support semester, exam date/timezone, syllabus/topics/skills, excluded scope and provisional missing instructions.
Version duration/sections/marks, optional questions, allowed tools/resources, navigation and scoring policies.
Verify cross-module isolation, configuration validation and history semantics without baking one semester's exam rules into code.
questions: Which identity mechanism is appropriate for the personal release?
What exact exam instructions/conventions should seed each profile?
stages.nonGoals: No public signup, billing, social presence or speculative monorepo.

stages.title: Import and review real sources, questions and solutions
stages.outcome: Import a small real question set and references, repair extraction, then publish an intact private version ready for practice.
exit: Support manual/pasted questions plus representative PDF/image inputs selected during architecture evaluation, with durable progress and retryable errors.
Preserve multipart nesting, shared context, marks, choices, equations, assets and original/source anchors; flag OCR and diagram ambiguity for review.
Keep prompt, key, rubric and source provenance distinct; label official, user-reviewed and AI-proposed solutions honestly.
Review/publish/retire revisions, detect exact duplicates, and show actionable repair state without changing old attempts.
questions: Which source formats are actually in the representative pack?
How are protected solutions and reserved papers separated at import?
stages.nonGoals: No direct Canvas integration, full-library bulk import or AI-written practice bank.

stages.title: Attempt multipart mathematical problems with durable working
stages.outcome: Attempt an intact ST2132 problem with readable notation, part dependencies and recoverable saved work.
exit: Keep assumptions/shared data visible and support part-level text/math working with accessible preview and optional confirmed image transcription.
Autosave/restore drafts, show saved/unsynced states and preserve immutable submissions across refresh/reconnect.
Separate skip, explicit blank, timeout and unreadable input; disclose when part-level feedback makes later work assisted.
Demonstrate estimation/testing/Fisher-information style problems without splitting them into unrelated drills.
questions: Which editor/input approach meets the owner's normal working habits?
When is feedback allowed within a dependent problem?
stages.nonGoals: No formal proof verification, generic handwriting promise or generated questions.

stages.title: Practise keyed choices and applied short answers
stages.outcome: Practise MCQs, multiple-select items and short applied responses with explicit answer/reasoning policy.
exit: Render original prompt/choice/diagram context and preserve selections and short-answer work.
Score single-choice and multiple-select against trusted keys and explicit exact-set/partial-credit rules.
Offer required, optional or sampled explanations by mode; optional blank reasoning is unassessed, not an inferred misconception.
Separate exam pick score, reasoning diagnosis, self-reported confidence and assistance, with keyboard behaviour that does not intercept text input.
questions: Which actual CS2100 choice-scoring policies need support?
stages.nonGoals: No unsupported partial-credit assumptions or topic mastery based on one correct choice.

stages.title: Capture MIPS programs and circuit-design answers
stages.outcome: Answer real CS2100 coding and design questions with preserved formatting and clear interpretation boundaries.
exit: Provide usable MIPS code input retaining whitespace and a readable view of supplied ISA/register/memory conventions.
Accept circuit drawing/images plus expression, truth table or confirmed structural description when suitable.
Require confirmation for ambiguous extracted labels/connections; preserve original evidence and offer review/self-marking paths.
Save/restore these responses with accessible narrow/keyboard interactions and without pretending a simulator or circuit checker ran.
questions: Which MIPS subset/conventions appear in the supplied questions?
Which diagram representation can the learner confirm accurately?
stages.nonGoals: No general-purpose IDE, circuit editor or simulator unless a subsequent scoped decision justifies it.

stages.title: Return source-grounded criterion marks with honest uncertainty
stages.outcome: A saved attempt produces versioned feedback with criterion marks, relevant authorised evidence and explicit unassessed parts.
exit: Deliver queued/marking/complete/provisional/failed states through the chosen bounded job path; retries do not duplicate attempts or learning events.
Scope retrieval by module, semester, source revision, access and solution-release policy; use full question context, rubric and answer.
Show criterion-level reasons, marks that sum correctly, actual checker coverage and valid anchored citations; abstain on inadequate evidence.
Support focused follow-up, disputed marks, versioned regrades and labelled self-assessment while preserving the original submission/result.
Evaluate unsupported feedback, valid alternatives and instruction attacks in documents/answers; protect other modules and reserved solutions.
questions: What quality thresholds and model routes passed the architecture-stage evaluation?
Which retrieval/source-precedence conflicts need explicit review?
stages.nonGoals: No claim that retrieval verifies proofs or that model confidence is calibrated reliability.

stages.title: Evaluate and deliver ST2132 mathematical marking
stages.outcome: Receive useful, evaluated partial-credit feedback on ST2132 derivations, tests, estimation and proofs.
exit: Assess assumptions, support/domain constraints, valid alternative derivations and criterion-specific logical obligations.
Handle test hypotheses/statistic/null distribution/rejection or p-value/conclusion as appropriate to the actual question.
Respect sample versus observation Fisher information and supplied parametrisations; apply declared follow-through/double-penalty rules.
Evaluate correct, partial, wrong and ambiguous representative answers; disclose provisional proof review and escalate/abstain when needed.
questions: Which official rubrics or reviewed alternatives establish the scoring contract?
stages.nonGoals: No exact-word matching, assumed regularity conditions or formal-verification claims.

stages.title: Evaluate and deliver CS2100 applied, MIPS and circuit feedback
stages.outcome: Receive evaluated CS2100 feedback that accepts valid alternatives and states exactly what was checked.
exit: Assess applied intermediate reasoning alongside trusted objective answer scores.
Review MIPS behaviour and required conventions; distinguish semantic review, assembly and executed tests in every result.
Assess confirmed circuit interpretation against functional/design criteria; valid equivalent forms are not rejected for differing appearance.
Evaluate representative correct/partial/wrong programs and circuits; keep unreadable or unchecked claims unresolved.
Decide whether a bounded deterministic checker is justified now; if adopted, test its limits and report coverage rather than treating tests as universal proof.
questions: Which assembly/execution/equivalence checks are reliable enough and worth their operational cost?
stages.nonGoals: No invented simulation results, arbitrary-language sandbox or general circuit-verification promise.

stages.title: Review weaknesses and plan study across both modules
stages.outcome: Turn assessed attempts into an explainable, manageable daily plan and retained mistake history.
exit: Track topic and skill evidence separately, preserving first/repeat, assisted/independent and immediate/delayed performance.
Retain mistakes and evidence-supported misconceptions, allow correction/dispute, and reopen recurring weaknesses without erasing history.
Schedule delayed retrieval and new exposure using one total time budget, task-duration estimates, excluded days and exam priorities.
Explain infeasible coverage and indivisible long-problem overruns; revise after missed days without unbounded backlog.
Ensure pending/failed/regraded assessments update learning evidence appropriately and exactly once.
questions: What review intervals and minimum independent evidence are justified initially?
stages.nonGoals: No uncalibrated recall percentages or mastery inferred from memorised MCQ variants.

stages.title: Run intact papers and timed mocks without solution leakage
stages.outcome: Take a real or assembled paper under its actual timing/navigation/marking rules and preserve work through interruption.
exit: Preserve sections, optional questions, marks, ordering, context and all supported answer formats in the selected profile.
Persist authoritative deadlines; refresh/navigation cannot reset them; define clear unsynced and expiry behaviour.
Reserve unseen papers and prevent protected answers leaking through ordinary practice, retrieval, hints, source previews or variants.
Release feedback at the right time and distinguish pending written marks from final scores; disclose prior exposure and coverage shortfalls.
questions: What are actual ST2132/CS2100 backtracking, pause and answer-release rules?
stages.nonGoals: No certified proctoring environment, invented exam mix or silent fallback to all-MCQ.

stages.title: Support personal notes, explain-back and short recall
stages.outcome: Capture contextual notes and practise definitions, formula conditions and explanations without displacing applied work.
exit: Create/search/edit/pin/delete personal notes with saved state, context links and deliberate recovery from deletion.
Offer explain-back on selected outcomes using scoped course evidence and honest feedback.
Offer short typed/revealed flashcards with self-rated versus checked evidence distinguished.
Keep personal notes separate from authoritative grading sources and ensure these activities do not substitute for proof/coding/design evidence.
questions: Which small recall deck is useful for the first two modules?
stages.nonGoals: No automatic publication of personal notes or requirement to justify every trivial fact at length.

stages.title: Validate and launch the personal revision release
stages.outcome: Use the complete personal loop on Cloudflare Pages with recoverable work, clear costs and known assessment limits.
exit: Exercise the full representative two-module journeys and record relevant acceptance evidence and remaining provisional checker limits.
Validate authentication/access, private-source handling, export/deletion/retention and source-revision lifecycle.
Verify interrupted imports/drafts/marking/timed papers, finite retry/budget limits, cancellation and operator diagnostics.
Check responsive/keyboard/zoom and human visual acceptance; set and measure asset, load and interaction budgets.
Provision authorised deployment configuration and document environment/rollback/runbook steps without committing secrets or adding unrequested recurring workers.
questions: What personal-use acceptance evidence, operating budget and deployment account access are needed?
stages.nonGoals: No public signup, monetisation or promise that all operation fits a free tier.

stages.title: Import accessible Canvas questions through an authorised connector
stages.outcome: Bring permitted Canvas material into the existing reviewed importer without altering quizzes or grades.
exit: Determine institution/account access and supported quiz formats using bounded sample reads.
Preview/select imports, preserve assets/provenance, paginate, handle missing keys/permissions and unsupported formats honestly.
Repeat imports detect revisions/duplicates; credentials stay out of source content and shared exports.
Provide a documented one-off browser acquisition fallback only for explicitly authorised visible content.
questions: Which Canvas APIs/exports are accessible to this student account?
stages.nonGoals: No hidden-key extraction, quiz submission, grade mutation or generic continuous browser scraper.

stages.title: Generate reviewed, source-supported practice variants
stages.outcome: Request new practice matching a skill/format and publish only answerable reviewed items.
exit: Generate from selected authorised sources with explicit type/difficulty/marks/time and bounded cost.
Attach proposed solution/rubric, provenance and family identity; check ambiguity, answer validity, constraints and near-duplicates.
Review/edit/reject before normal scheduling and honour reserved-paper protection.
Distinguish close-variant performance from independent novel transfer and generated content from official questions.
questions: Which generation tasks pass mathematical/program/circuit quality gates?
stages.nonGoals: No automatic publication of unverified keys or claims of predicting future exam content.

stages.title: Extend assessment to essays with module-specific rubrics
stages.outcome: Revise an essay-based module using defensible rubric feedback rather than generic keyword scores.
exit: Select an actual target module and reviewed exemplar/rubric set before implementation.
Support extended drafting/submission and criteria for argument, evidence, accuracy and structure as required.
Accept multiple defensible positions, cite relevant sources, preserve uncertainty and evaluate challenged marks.
Integrate the essay skill/time profile with existing papers and learning evidence without diluting the first two modules.
questions: Which future module and essay conventions justify this expansion?
stages.nonGoals: No universal essay marker or immediate ST2132/CS2100 release dependency.

stages.title: Evaluate useful recall and exam-readiness forecasts
stages.outcome: Show only forecasts that improve planning and are supported by enough independent learning evidence.
exit: Define precisely what is forecast and distinguish item recall from full-paper performance across skills.
Evaluate calibration with delayed independent outcomes and communicate sparse-data/uncertainty limitations.
Compare against the baseline evidence-only plan and avoid introducing misleading precision.
Record the decision to ship, revise or withhold forecasts; retain useful evidence-based states in every case.
questions: Is there enough real data to validate a forecast at all?
stages.nonGoals: No untested exam percentages or model self-confidence displayed as empirical probability.

stages.title: Share selected module content with an invited group
stages.outcome: Invite students to approved content while preserving each learner's private work and sources.
exit: Define owner/editor/learner permissions and separate source visibility from question visibility.
Implement explicit publishing/invites, independent progress, private supplements, content corrections and reports.
Verify isolation through retrieval/citations, direct links, exports, regrades and retired content, not just visible navigation.
Set per-user/project budgets and agreed retention/removal policies; run a small monitored pilot with documented failure recovery.
questions: Which materials can be shared, and how many pilot students fit the budget?
stages.nonGoals: No public signup or implicit sharing of notes, answers, credentials or every source in the owner's library.

stages.title: Prepare optional public onboarding and sustainable operation
stages.outcome: Decide whether and how broader free access can run within demonstrated service and content constraints.
exit: Use pilot evidence to decide quotas, abuse controls, moderation/report handling and operating budget stop behaviour.
Define onboarding, content ownership/licensing and removal policies, service diagnostics and release/rollback ownership.
Measure performance/concurrency and privacy/recovery under realistic usage before opening signup.
Retain saved work and explain service limits when new expensive jobs are unavailable.
questions: Should access remain invite-only if budget or content constraints make public signup unsuitable?
stages.nonGoals: No billing, mandatory social features, or public rollout before pilot evidence.

stages.title: Resolve the lint toolchain's transitive minimatch advisory
stages.outcome: Keep the lint toolchain supported while resolving the known glob-matching advisory without an unreviewed transitive major override.
exit: Reproduce npm audit for GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 and determine actual reachability in local/CI linting; it currently affects development dependencies, not the React production dependency tree.
Prefer upstream compatible fixes; if considering an override or alternate linter, evaluate changed glob semantics and all affected configuration paths.
Run clean-install formatting/lint/typecheck/build and relevant tooling checks; document the supported dependency decision.
Do not describe a dev-only advisory as a deployed application exploit or use npm audit fix --force blindly.
questions: Have ESLint/typescript-eslint released a compatible fixed dependency range by implementation time?
stages.nonGoals: No forced package downgrades or arbitrary major dependency overrides solely to silence audit output.
